resources.string: Kaam complete hua, aapka kaam complete hua!
Ready. Open Sudha Daily Orders, then press Start.

Automates the daily order-entry task in the Sudha Daily Orders app. It only reads and taps screens inside the package you configure, keeps a per-day ledger of processed retailers, and never submits the same order twice. The automation itself never uses the network; the app goes online only when you ask it to download a sound of your own.

Name the Sudha Daily Orders package. Sutara reads the number of retailers from the app\'s own “Total Customers” line; the figure below is used only when the app shows none. Progress is saved per day, so a pause or a restart never repeats a retailer.
Retailers expected (only if the app shows no total)
Switch to the Sudha app now — capturing in 10 seconds…
No capture yet. Make sure the Sudha app is open and the accessibility service is ON.
Choose a chat app to paste the capture into.
Some capture files could not be deleted.
Not installed (%1$s) — use Capture screen (Backstage) to read the real package name
Asleep — tap, then switch on Sutara
Only IDs shaped SMR followed by digits are ever touched. Distributor IDs such as SM65 and plain numbers are ignored.
Enter the exact Sudha Daily Orders package name.
No app with that package is installed on this device.

Today\'s SUCCESS, SKIPPED and ERROR records will be cleared so every retailer becomes eligible again. This is refused while an order is in flight.\n\nWhat Sutara has learned about the Sudha app (renamed labels, the roster) is NOT erased. That has its own button in her notebook.
When a run ends, a card covers the screen with the day\'s numbers: placed, skipped, to check. It makes no sound. Tap it to close it.
Full-screen card when a run ends
This is only a preview — nothing went wrong. A real one shows what stopped the run.
Any image or GIF on the phone; it takes Sutara\'s place on the card. Clear brings her back.
Saved — press the preview to see it.
This phone has no file picker available.
AI employee · zero salary · zero chai breaks
Employee of the month, every month

When the Sudha app is updated and renames something, Sutara compares the new screen with the words the bot relies on and writes down the new name. She matches by meaning and spelling on the phone itself — a rule book, not a cloud AI — and when she is not sure she asks instead of guessing. Reset never clears this page.
Updated since she last worked with it: %1$s. She is watching for changes.
Nothing yet — the Sudha app still uses the names the bot was built with.
WAITING FOR YOUR OK — not used until you allow it

Sutara thinks %1$s is now labelled “%2$s”.\n\nIf you allow it, the bot will press “%2$s” where it used to press “%3$s”. Only allow it if you have looked at the Sudha app and that is really the same button.
No report — nothing has stopped her yet.
Every learned name will be erased and the bot will look for the original labels again. Today\'s ledger is not touched. Use this only if she learned something wrong.
Notebook cleared. The bot is back to the original labels.
There is no report to send yet.
WhatsApp is not installed — choose another app.
The report could not be shared.
Allow notifications so Sutara can tell you when the work is done or when she needs help.
Work finished, something learned, or help needed.
The Sudha app renamed it. She has adapted and carried on.
Noted in her notebook for next time.
%1$s seems to be called “%2$s” now. She will not press it until you allow it in her notebook.
Sutara is stuck — the Sudha app has changed
Sutara stopped and needs a human
Sutara: three retailers in a row failed
Auto-Dialogues on: a film dialogue after each order, a sad one after an error. No songs.
Ask Sutara… (haal? kyon ruki? skip list?)
Sawaal type karne ke liye pehle Pause dabaiye.
Nobody has been skipped for an empty order list or for want of an order on T-1 to T-5.
The list of skipped retailers is cleared.

Sir, %1$s tak ho chuka hai. Start dabate hi uske baad wale se shuru karungi.
Lock is on. The next song that plays will stay.
Song unlocked. Upbeat after an order, sad after an error.
Sutara places the daily orders for you
Starts from the top of the list

Hindi film songs of the 80s and 90s, streamed from YouTube while Sutara works. Sound only, no video. An upbeat song starts with the first order and the songs keep coming while orders go through. If a retailer ends in an error the music cross-fades to a sad one, and back again at the next order. Lock song, on the floating panel, keeps the song that is playing and repeats it.

On: when a new page has come up and is still, the bot goes on at once instead of waiting a fixed time. Placing the order and paying keep the old timing. Off: everything keeps the old timing. Takes effect at the next Start. Not yet tried on a phone: watch the first few retailers, and switch this off if anything looks wrong. With the phone\'s animations off (Developer options → Window and Transition animation scale → Off) it is a little quicker still.
None. Songs are found on YouTube.
Open the song on YouTube, tap Share, Copy link, and paste it here. A direct https link to a sound file (mp3, m4a, ogg) or an internet-radio stream works too.
Added. Playing half a minute of it.
The list is full, or the song is already in it.

Needs internet: about 1 MB of data a minute while music plays. The app carries no songs of its own; it plays what YouTube answers for “90s bollywood dance hits” and similar searches, so a song can now and then be from another year. If the music stops working after a YouTube change, the app needs an update; ordering is not affected.
Music is switched off. Turn it on in Sutara, under Music while working.
Music starts with the first order.
Optional: your own songs. While a list below has songs, only those are played for that mood.

On: no songs. When an order is placed a rousing Hindi film dialogue is said; when a retailer ends in an error, or the run stops, a sad or dramatic one. Each is a short clip found on YouTube on the day, heard once for at most 20 seconds; a dialogue that is still being heard is not cut short by the next order. Off: the songs again. The microphone button on the floating panel is the same switch. Which clips YouTube answers with cannot be chosen from here, so try the two buttons below first.
%1$d%% of what is behind shows through the open panel.

Left: more solid, easiest to read. Right: more see-through. The words are never thinned; they get a pale edge so they can be read over the app behind. Folded, the panel is always a bare ring with nothing inside. Takes effect the next time the panel is opened.
